newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia MinFins off on profit-taking,U.S. bond fall.
newsitem.headline: Russia MinFins off on profit-taking,U.S. bond fall.

text.p: Russian MinFin bonds slipped on Thursday on profit-taking and following a slip in U.S. Treasuries, dealers said.
"The fall started in the morning on profit-taking," said Pavel Afanasyev, an Avtobank dealer. "After a fall of about 0.2-0.3 percent the market hit a support level and rose a bit."
U.S. Treasury securities prices ended lower on Wednesday after the expected outcome of the central bank meeting was met with a rise in bearish sentiment.
Sergei Seregin, chief trader at Aljba-Alliance bank, said short positions opened by Moscow banks also pushed prices down.
Dealers said they were waiting for U.S. payroll figures.
"The market is waiting for the figures to decide in which direction to move," Seregin said.

The figure, which arrived after Moscow dealers had made their comments, pointed to further labour market tightness. Jobless claims for the week ended February 1 fell to 325,000 from a revised 337,000 the previous week. Economists in a Reuters poll had forecast 347,000 new claims.
Afanasyev forecast a further slip on Friday as banks were reluctant to leave long positions open over the week-end.
